title: Butterflies
objective: After this level you can explain how a caterpillar becomes a butterfly.
summary: Butterflies pass through egg, larva, pupa and adult. In the chrysalis most caterpillar tissue dissolves, and imaginal discs build the wings, legs and eyes.

cards.headline: Inside a chrysalis, a caterpillar digests itself.
cards.body: It releases enzymes that dissolve most of its own body into what scientists call caterpillar soup. Out of that soup comes an animal with wings, new legs and new eyes. So how do you build a butterfly from soup?

events.label: Egg: a monarch egg hatches about four days after it’s laid
Larva, the caterpillar: grows from under 1 cm to about 5 cm
Pupa, the chrysalis: the body is rebuilt inside
Adult: the winged butterfly climbs out

cards.headline: Soup with a blueprint
cards.body: The meltdown isn’t chaos. While the caterpillar was still inside its egg, it grew small groups of cells called imaginal discs, one for each adult part it would need: eyes, wings, legs and more. In the chrysalis, the discs survive, feed on the soup around them and divide fast. In a fruit fly, a wing disc can grow from about 50 cells to more than 50,000. The caterpillar carried the plans for its future the whole time.

cards.fact: Four stages add up to complete metamorphosis.
cards.context: Going through all four, egg, larva, pupa and adult, is what biologists call complete metamorphosis. The caterpillar and the butterfly look like two different animals, but they’re one insect at two ends of the same process. The wings you admire were packed away as tiny discs inside the caterpillar.

mascot.line: Hold on to these stages. Level 59's mosquitoes go through larva and pupa too.

cards.headline: Butterflies: transformed
learned: Four stages: egg, larva, pupa, adult
Most caterpillar tissue dissolves into soup
Imaginal discs build wings, legs and eyes

questions.prompt: What is the pupa stage of a butterfly also called?

options.label: The larva
options.rationale: The larva is the caterpillar, the stage before.

options.label: The instar
options.rationale: An instar is a stage between a caterpillar’s molts.

options.label: The nymph
options.rationale: Butterflies don’t have a nymph stage.

questions.explanation: A butterfly’s pupa is the chrysalis, the stage between caterpillar and adult.

questions.prompt: If a caterpillar dissolves inside its chrysalis, how does the butterfly get built?

options.label: Imaginal discs survive and grow into adult parts
The caterpillar’s legs stretch into wings
options.rationale: Wings come from their own discs, not from legs.

options.label: The chrysalis shell turns into the butterfly
options.rationale: The chrysalis is a casing the adult leaves behind.

options.label: The soup hardens into a new body at random
options.rationale: The rebuild follows the discs’ plan.

questions.explanation: Groups of cells called imaginal discs, grown before the caterpillar hatched, survive and use the soup to build the adult.

questions.prompt: Level 51 said an adult insect’s wings sit on its thorax. Where do a butterfly’s wings come from?

options.label: They are folded inside the egg from the start
options.rationale: The egg holds a caterpillar, not wings.

options.label: They grow out of the caterpillar’s back each molt
options.rationale: Caterpillars have no wings at all.

options.label: The adult grows them after leaving the chrysalis
options.rationale: They are already built when the adult climbs out.

options.label: Wing discs grow into wings inside the chrysalis

questions.explanation: Imaginal discs for the wings survive in the chrysalis and grow into the adult’s wings.
